I'm a beginning woodworker, but I have a some experience with machining in metal and plastics and some experience with framing and construction. I'm going to do more woodworking in the coming years and am looking for advice on tools to buy. I can afford to spend up to about CDN$2000 (US$1500) in the near term, and a bit more down the road. But I'm flexible on that and am prepared to spend more to get better quality, if it's worth it for hobby woodworking.

My thinking at the moment is that I would buy a decent table saw and get rid of my radial arm saw. I seems to me that, with the table saw (and the chop saw I already have), I won't really need the radial saw anymore, and it would free up a lot of space. Assuming this is a good basic plan, it looks like I could easily spend the entire budget on just the table saw, to get a good one. I'm okay with that, as I would rather over-buy than under-buy. But I'm wondering about other things, like a planer or a jointer. With the table saw and my router, can I get buy without a jointer? A planer seems pretty necessary. Will I regret it if I economize on the table saw so I can afford a planer, too, or am I better off getting the best table saw I can afford and adding the planer later?

For reference, this is what I have now (in addition to a pretty good collection of hand and mechanical tools):

* Radial arm saw (10"; rough cut blade; cabinet blade; wobbly-type dado blade) * Chop saw (12"; non-compound) * Band saw (free standing; tilt-head) * Circular saw (8") * Jig saw * Router (Bosch 2-1/4 HP fixed/plung) * Drill press (free standing; 16" throw) * Belt/disc sander (table top) * Palm sander * Lathe-mill combination machine * Shop-vac with some dust-collection accessories (but not a lot) * Three-phase 220 power in the shop

My shop is a one-car garage which also holds a motorcyle and my wife's kiln, so space is at a bit of a premium right now. But I don't want that to affect the decision too much because we plan to move in a few years to a place with more shop space. I'm okay with pulling stuff out of the shop while I work when necessary, in the meantime.
Advice on table saw and other machinery (long question)

I'm a fan of going big on the table saw. It will rip better than your arm saw can and between it and the chop (I assume it's a good miter saw?) You might be able to retire the arm saw for space. Although an arm is nice for quick cuts.
